correctness.rationale: For the 8-vertex unfilled bouquet graph E={01,12,20,03,34,40,05,56,67,70}, in a strict vertex filtration an oriented incidence (v,w) is selected exactly if w is the only earlier neighbor of v. Independently exhausted 8!=40320 orders yielding 345 generated masks and 493 faces including empty, f=(20,108,220,144). Reproduced the prescribed sequence of face-toggle discrete Morse pairings: 239 pairs; the entire 492-vertex directed Hasse diagram topologically sorts; unmatched exactly one vertex and 13 three-faces, no intermediate dimension, giving integral wedge^13 S^3 by Forman. Independent reconstruction of each of 16 automorphism signed fixed-face Lefschetz sums then Hopf trace yields character rows 13/-9, -7/3,5/-1,-7/3,5/-1 with class multiplicities 1,2,1,2,2 for square fixed/reversed. No integral equivariant lattice is claimed.

It does not establish this particular mixed three-petal cactus or its full symmetry character. Published two-petal triangle+cycle and uniform square-bouquet results are structurally different; neither furnishes the 16-character data for two interchangeable triangles plus an independently reversed square. Exact finite topology and rational representation survive comparison as best-of-knowledge.

value.rationale: The eight-vertex graph is a canonical smallest three-petal mixed bouquet with a nontrivial two-triangle interchange and one 4-cycle. The observed persistence of 13 summands while sphere dimension jumps from 1 to 3 is a motivated first mixed-gluing boundary, and the complete rational automorphism character adds independently usable representation data not determined by a wedge rank. A natural finite complete classification need not be an all-cactus theorem.
